methods: substituting the line into the plane
statement: Find the point of intersection of the line $\mathbf{r}=(1,2,3)+t(2,-1,1)$ with the plane $x+2y+3z=14$.
solution: A general point on the line is $(1+2t,\,2-t,\,3+t)$. Substituting into the plane: $(1+2t)+2(2-t)+3(3+t)=14$, i.e. $1+2t+4-2t+9+3t=14$, so $14+3t=14$, giving $t=0$. The intersection point is $(1,2,3)$.
hints: Write a general point on the line.
Substitute its coordinates into the plane equation.
Solve for t and read off the point.
